variants.text: Don't move in together early if you can avoid it. Once you're living together, leaving gets mixed up with rent, housing, furniture, sleep, all the boring stuff. That makes it much harder to tell whether you're staying because you want the relationship or because getting out is a pain in the ass. Housing can force the issue sometimes; I'm talking about when you actually have a choice.

Pick a date to check in before something goes wrong. Otherwise “we'll see how it goes” can turn into never asking how it's going until one of you is already done. I don't mean a formal relationship performance review. Just a day when both people know they're allowed to say, actually, this part isn't working for me.

I can want someone and still have no idea whether I should build a life with her. Those aren't different degrees of the same decision. I can be completely sure I want the romance and still not know what kind of co-parent she'd be, whether we'd want the same community, or whether we'd even like sharing ordinary life for years.

One of the stupid things my brain can do is turn “I'm taking a chance on her” into “she's the right person” after we've been together for a while. Based on what? Sometimes I actually learned something. Sometimes nothing changed except that now I'm attached, and the new certainty is just harder for me to question.
